prompt:
Edit the primary reference image into a photorealistic finished prototype concept for the Korean "300 Seconds" Fold Wing Buddy learning companion. Primary reference is the original v4 cream and olive robot desk product. The other reference images show actual available hardware and must guide the design: the long Britz BA-R9 soundbar, MAX7219 8x8 dot matrix, blue touch boards, 5V addressable RGB strips, metal JX servos. Maintain the original warm child study desk, open Korean math workbook, rounded cream matte PLA shells and muted olive accents, phone cradle left of central head, symmetrical raised articulated arms with rounded fixed fingers. Make it look like a plausible assembled maker prototype with fine PLA layers, service seams and small screws, not a futuristic impossible appliance. High quality natural product photography, landscape 3:2.
USER'S LATEST CHANGE IS ESSENTIAL: use EXACTLY TWO physically distinct SQUARE 8-by-8 monochrome LED matrices for the left and right eyes. Each square has exactly 8 columns and 8 rows of round pixel dots, subtle visible unlit dots. Coarse friendly smiling eye patterns in warm amber/red points, no OLED, no smooth high resolution curved eye graphics, no single shared matrix. Position both square modules side by side behind separate square smoked windows within a rounded dark face inset. This is planned quantity two even though only one was photographed. Mount one small Raspberry Pi V2 camera aperture centered above/between the eyes. One small microphone capsule aperture on the upper head, NOT a microphone array.
Replace the small fictional fabric belly speaker with the REAL long black BA-R9 soundbar integrated into the FRONT OF THE WIDE BASE: preserve long rectangular black metal grille, its 400 mm width proportion and small right end volume knob/headphone ports, recognizable like reference. Cream mounting frame and olive lower base surround it. Total product base about 650-700 mm wide so the complete soundbar fits naturally; head sits above it. Do not shrink the soundbar into a tiny belly speaker. No extra speaker in head.
Two arms, each with only TWO motorized revolute joints: base yaw and upper hand pitch, implemented with realistic standard-size black/silver metal servo housings, brackets and routed cable sleeving; four servos total visible or partially shrouded. Preserve modest arm proportions. Rounded fixed olive fingers have no motorized finger joints. Each palm has a SHALLOW FLAT frosted circular RGB LED diffuser fed by existing 5V addressable LED strips. Show softly glowing RGB status lights, not reading spotlights. NO movable zoom lens, no lens actuator, no focus mechanism, no projector, no narrow beams onto workbook, no claims of optical spot/wide functions: those parts are not owned. Add short visible rows of six discrete diffused RGB status dots along each forearm, with subdued brightness.
Six capacitive touch pads mounted behind the cream/olive base skin, arranged three small understated fingertip touch targets on each side, visible as six simple recessed circular markers; hide the actual blue PCBs internally. Jetson Nano with heatsink, PCA9685 board, USB audio dongle, power converter and battery fit in a deeper ventilated rear/base electronics compartment, represented by credible rear vent slots and removable service lid seams, with no visible unprotected wires. These are packaging concepts, not verified working electronics. Do not show battery charger/balancer as part of the operational robot. Keep phone and workbook as context.
Remove ALL old technical arrows and labels from the original, including J1 YAW, J2 PITCH, LENS ACTUATOR, SPOT and WIDE. No floating annotations, no component inventory collage, no exploded view. One clean three-quarter front hero shot showing entire prototype, both eyes clearly visible and no cropping arms. Preserve cozy Korean home educational mood.
limitations: Concept rendering only; dimensions, packing, pixel grid accuracy and operation are not verified.
Two matrix eyes are a user-approved design plan; photographed inventory remains one matrix.
Reading-light optics and lens actuators are not in the confirmed BOM; palms show RGB status lighting.
